In order to cast the molten material created inside the material, various blocks are used to route the molten material into molds. These are called §6Basins§r.

The molds themselves are shaped in an §6Anvil§r using the two§a§r combination§r §rslots available in the top of the anvil GUI. 

There are three types of Basins:

§6Shallow foundry basins§r, which receive molten material from channels, either from above via an outlet, or directly from the sides. The foundry basin must be fitted with a mold before it can receive material. Once it has filled up with enough material to satisfy the current mold, it will begin cooling. Hoppers and conveyors can be attached to both basin types to pull the finished products from them, otherwise they must be right-clicked to extract the finished products, and won't accept any more material until they have been emptied. 

§6Foundry basins§r, which receive molten material from channels, filling up material. Once enough material has flowed into the basin, it will begin cooling the material. Foundry basins require molds to be inserted to function, otherwise they will not receive material. Unlike the shallow foundry basins, they will not receive material from their sides, and must be poured into from above with an outlet. 

§6Foundry storage basins§r, which receive molten metal but do not cast them. Instead they're used for storage of these molten metals for later use. 

Note that you can sneak right click on a §6Basin§r block with a §9Screwdriver§r to extract the mold from it.
